title: Enterprise Bootstrap Theme
description:
Components of the Enterprise Bootstrap Theme, plus the A2UI basic catalog's components and functions, which this catalog re-exports. Every data property accepts a literal, a {"path": …} binding or a {"call": …} function call to one of this catalog's functions; a <request>Result property accepts only a binding. Each event a component emits has an on<Event> action property. A component whose events or requests carry a payload has one binding-only eventData property: bind it to a path, and the component writes each event's payload to <path>/<channel>, and each request to <path>/<request>, before sending the matching action, so read that path in the action's context; the context is resolved after the write. A request's on<Request> action asks you for data: answer with updateDataModel at the path bound to its <request>Result property, with a value matching the $defs entry its description names, once per request. A two-way value property receives the user's changes at its bound path. Some two-way components also send an action when the value changes; that action carries no payload of its own, so read the new value through the path bound to value.

- ChatDock: ChatDock. Show a running conversation with a message input, so the user can talk to the agent inside the surface. For a single free-text answer use TextField; for a static transcript use List with Text.
- ColumnsPicker: Columns Picker. Let the user choose how many text columns a page or section uses, from presets that preview it. For page margins use MarginsPicker; for paper size use SizesPicker.
- CronPicker: CRON Picker. Let the user build a recurring schedule as a CRON expression, with presets and a readable summary. For a single date use DatePicker; for a length of time use DurationPicker.
- DatePicker: Date Picker. Let the user pick one calendar date from a popup calendar, with optional limits. For a date and a time use DateTimeInput; for a fiscal month or quarter use PeriodPicker. Use it to edit, schedule a scalar of exactly 1 item.
- DurationPicker: Duration Picker. Let the user enter a length of time in units such as days, hours and minutes. For a time of day use TimePicker; for a recurring schedule use CronPicker.
- FontDropdown: Font Dropdown. Let the user choose a font family from a list that previews each font in its own typeface. For choices that are not fonts use ChoicePicker; for a free-text font name use TextField.
- GraphLegend: Graph Legend. Explain the node and edge types of a graph or diagram, with colours, icons and optional counts. For a plain key-value list use List with Text; it is not a legend for numeric chart series.
- LayoutPicker: Layout Picker. Let the user choose an automatic layout algorithm for a graph or diagram, shown as thumbnails. For choices that are not layout algorithms use ChoicePicker.
- LineEndingPicker: Line Ending Picker. Let the user choose an arrowhead or other end marker for a line or connector in a diagram. For a line's dash pattern use LineTypePicker; for its thickness use LineWidthPicker.
- LineShapePicker: Line Shape Picker. Let the user choose the routing shape of a connector in a diagram, such as straight or curved. For a line's dash pattern use LineTypePicker; for its end markers use LineEndingPicker.
- LineTypePicker: Line Type Picker. Let the user choose a line's dash pattern, such as solid, dashed or dotted, with a preview. For a line's thickness use LineWidthPicker; for its routing shape use LineShapePicker.
- LineWidthPicker: Line Width Picker. Let the user choose a line or border thickness from a list that previews each width. For a line's dash pattern use LineTypePicker; for an arbitrary number use Slider.
- MarginsPicker: Margins Picker. Let the user choose page margins from named presets such as Normal, Narrow and Wide. For paper size use SizesPicker; for line and paragraph spacing use SpacingPicker.
- OrientationPicker: Orientation Picker. Let the user choose portrait or landscape page orientation, shown as two page icons. For any other choice between a few options use ChoicePicker.
- PeriodPicker: Period Picker. Let the user pick a reporting period such as a month, quarter, half or year from a grid. For a single calendar date use DatePicker; for an agile sprint use SprintPicker.
- Ruler: Ruler. Show a measuring ruler in px, cm, mm or inches beside a canvas or document area. For choosing a number use Slider or TextField; a ruler only displays a scale.
- SizesPicker: Sizes Picker. Let the user choose a paper or page size, such as Letter, Legal or A4, from named presets. For page margins use MarginsPicker; for text columns use ColumnsPicker.
- SkeletonLoader: Skeleton Loader. Hold the place of content that is still loading, shaped like text, a card, an avatar or a table. For a status the user should read use Text; replace the loader as soon as the content arrives.
- SpacingPicker: Spacing Picker. Let the user choose line and paragraph spacing for text from named presets such as Single or Double. For page margins use MarginsPicker; for a free numeric value use Slider.
- SprintPicker: Sprint Picker. Let the user pick an agile sprint from a list computed from a start date and a sprint length. For a fiscal month or quarter use PeriodPicker; for a single calendar date use DatePicker.
- StickyNote: Sticky Note. Let the user write or read one short free-form note, styled as a coloured sticky note. For a labelled form input use TextField; for read-only prose use Text. Use it to author, summarize a document of exactly 1 item.
- TimePicker: Time Picker. Let the user pick a time of day, in a 12- or 24-hour clock, optionally with a timezone. For a date and time together use DateTimeInput; for a length of time use DurationPicker.
- TimezonePicker: Timezone Picker. Let the user pick an IANA timezone from a searchable list that shows each zone's offset. For a time of day with its own timezone selector use TimePicker.
- ToolColorPicker: Tool Color Picker. Let the user pick a drawing colour for a pen, marker, pencil, highlighter or brush from a small palette. For choosing between named options that are not colours use ChoicePicker.
- TreeView: Tree View. Show a hierarchy the user browses, expands and selects from, such as folders or categories. For a flat list without nesting use List; to pick one or more options use ChoicePicker. Use it to browse, navigate, inspect a hierarchy of 1 to 20000 items.
- WorkspaceShell: WorkspaceShell. Show several named canvases as tabs the user can select, pin, close or create, with a history scrubber. For simple tabbed content without canvas actions use Tabs.

showTranscript.description:
Show the transcript above the input. Default true.

The transcript is a FIXED-height scrolling region, so the dock never
changes size as the conversation grows. Set false for a pure input bar
where history lives in a separate panel.
